SU4_fixed_space.displayed_fixed_basis: A, B, Re(dz1 dz2 dz3 dz4), Im(dz1 dz2 dz3 dz4)

linearized_kernel.kernel_decomposition: T_F(SO(10).F)[20] direct_sum R*F[1] direct_sum Re(Lambda^(4,0) C^5)[10]

local_component_argument.applies_at_minus_F: The residuals are quadratic, so the same derivative-rank and slice argument applies separately at -F.
local_component_argument.step_1_slice: The compact SO(10) slice theorem puts every sufficiently nearby orbit into the orthogonal normal slice at F.
local_component_argument.step_2_IFT: On the unit normal slice d(Pi4125) has rank 179, so 179 independent residual coordinates solve the 179 massive variables uniquely as an analytic graph over the real C^5 kernel.
local_component_argument.step_3_equivariance: Uniqueness and U(5)-invariance make the graph U(5)-equivariant.
local_component_argument.step_4_transitivity: SU(5) acts transitively on the unit sphere in C^5; a nonzero kernel coordinate is rotated, with phase fixed, to c*Re(dz1...dz4).
local_component_argument.step_5_fixed_slice: Its SU(4) stabilizer fixes the graph point.  The exact fixed-space calculation puts it in the phase-fixed A,B,C slice.
local_component_argument.step_6_obstruction: The two exact projector identities imply c=0, contradicting a nonzero C^5 coordinate.  Unit norm then leaves only F locally.
local_component_argument.theorem: There are neighborhoods U_plus and U_minus on the unit sphere whose common projector-zero sets are exactly U_plus intersect SO(10).F and U_minus intersect SO(10).(-F).
local_component_argument.theorem_scope: qualitative local neighborhoods; no explicit radius

verdict: The signed Kahler-square orbits are exact isolated local components of the normalized Phi projector-zero locus.  No infinitesimal or nonlinear branch can emanate from either orbit.  A disconnected component far from both signed orbits is not excluded, so the global Phi lemma and G3 remain open.
